article_notes: 40 dogs naturally infected with B. canis canis (Zagreb, Croatia; smear and PCR, PCR-confirmed in all 40) and 30 healthy controls. All infected dogs had SIRS. 29 uncomplicated, 11 complicated (6 one complication, 5 MODS); 4 deaths, all in the MODS group. Anaemia: 17 non-anaemic, 16 mild, 6 moderate, 1 severe (severe not analysed). Markers (SOD, GPx, catalase in whole blood; TAS and MDA in serum) measured at admission. Group values are median (IQR); Mann-Whitney U; significance is given mainly by superscript letters (P < 0.05 for Tables 3-5) plus thresholds in the text, so most p-values are thresholds ('<0.01', '<0.05') or '>0.05' for non-significant results (no exact p printed). Complicated vs uncomplicated (pooled 11 vs 29) was not tested, only the one-complication and MODS subgroups. Groups are very small (MODS n=5, deaths n=4), and S2/S3/S4 overlap heavily. Table 6 TAS-HCT coefficient printed as -0.62 without a star, probably a typo. Table 6 correlations with urea, creatinine, bilirubin, ALT, AP and CPK were not extracted (correlations between markers and other laboratory analytes, not with a severity measure); Table 8 marker-marker correlations not extracted. MDA was previously reported in this population (Crnogaj et al., cited); possible cohort overlap with other Zagreb B. canis studies. GPx values are printed with comma thousands separators and are copied as printed. skipped_infected_vs_healthy = 5 markers compared between babesiosis and control dogs (Table 2 and control column of Table 3).

severity_definitions.label: one complication vs uncomplicated
severity_definitions.definition: Complicated babesiosis split into dogs with a single organ dysfunction and MODS, using Table 1 criteria (renal: creatinine >180 μmol/L; respiratory: dyspnoea/nasal discharge or radiographic pulmonary oedema; hepatic: ALT >176 U/L, AP >360 U/L and bilirubin >100 μmol/L; muscular: CPK >600 U/L; CNS: modified Glasgow coma scale <9). Uncomplicated = none of the listed complications. Pancreatitis and secondary infection were noted as additional, not main, complications.
severity_definitions.quote: On the basis of clinical manifestations and laboratory data the affected dogs were divided into two groups: uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis, whereas the complicated group was further subdivided into those with one complication and the MODS group, due to the criteria listed in Table 1.

severity_definitions.label: MODS vs uncomplicated
severity_definitions.definition: MODS = two or more organ dysfunctions by Table 1 criteria; uncomplicated = no listed complication. Of the 5 MODS dogs, 4 died.
severity_definitions.quote: In dogs with complicated babesiosis, 6 (54.55%) had single organ dysfunction and 5 (45.45%) dogs had MODS.

severity_definitions.label: MODS vs one complication
severity_definitions.definition: MODS (two or more organ dysfunctions) vs single organ dysfunction, within complicated babesiosis, by Table 1 criteria.
severity_definitions.quote: In dogs with complicated babesiosis, 6 (54.55%) had single organ dysfunction and 5 (45.45%) dogs had MODS.

severity_definitions.label: lethal outcome (died vs survived)
severity_definitions.definition: Death despite treatment; follow-up horizon not stated. All 4 deaths were dogs with MODS (mortality 10%). Analysed as Kendall tau-b correlation of each marker with outcome.
severity_definitions.quote: Treatment was successful in all dogs without development of any complications as well as in 7 cases of complicated babesiosis, while 4 dogs with MODS died despite treatment (mortality rate 10%).

severity_definitions.label: anaemic vs non-anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Anaemia by HCT: non-anaemic HCT >37%; anaemic HCT <=37% (mild 30–37%, moderate 18–29%, severe <18%).
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: moderately anaemic vs mildly anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Moderate anaemia HCT 18–29% vs mild anaemia HCT 30–37%. The single severely anaemic dog was not analysed.
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: mildly anaemic vs non-anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Mild anaemia HCT 30–37% vs non-anaemic HCT >37% (pairwise comparison in Table 5).
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: moderately anaemic vs non-anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Moderate anaemia HCT 18–29% vs non-anaemic HCT >37% (pairwise comparison in Table 5).
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: haematocrit (continuous degree of anaemia)
severity_definitions.definition: Spearman correlation of each marker with admission HCT (%) in the 40 infected dogs; lower HCT = more severe anaemia.
severity_definitions.quote: Also, there was a significant positive correlation of HCT with GPx and SOD, whereas significant negative correlation of HCT with MDA (Table 6).
